s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of generalized skin lesions and jaundice following a surgical procedure
salient_findings: Generalized painful fluid-filled skin lesions
Yellow scleral discoloration
Fever following removal of a tibial implant
Development of pruritus and fluid-filled rashes after antibiotic use
Icterus with elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels
key_facts: 22-year-old man
15-day history of generalized painful fluid-filled skin lesions
7 days of yellow scleral discoloration
1 month of fever following removal of a tibial implant
History of tibial fracture treated with internal fixation
Surgical-site infection and persistent fever after implant removal
Initial treatment with paracetamol without relief
Development of generalized pruritus after starting ciprofloxacin
Denial of angioedema, dyspnea, abdominal distention, lower-limb swelling, hematemesis, melena, altered sensorium, alcohol use, or immunocompromise
Afebrile with stable vital signs on examination
Icterus without pallor, clubbing, cyanosis, lymphadenopathy, or dehydration
Multiple generalized vesicles and bullae with non-hemorrhagic crusts over the trunk and extremities
Leukocyte count 18,520/mm3 with neutrophils 64%, lymphocytes 22%, and eosinophils 12%
Elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Generalized painful fluid-filled skin lesions and mucosal involvement following ciprofloxacin use

shortlist.label: DRESS syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Fever, rash, and systemic involvement after ciprofloxacin initiation, with elevated eosinophils

shortlist.label: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid onset of generalized pustular rash after ciprofloxacin use, with neutrophilia and eosinophilia

shortlist.label: Drug-induced liver injury
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels after ciprofloxacin use, suggesting hepatotoxicity

shortlist.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe skin lesions and mucosal involvement, with potential for life-threatening complications

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including generalized painful fluid-filled skin lesions, yellow scleral discoloration, fever, and elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels, are consistent with DRESS syndrome, which is a severe skin and systemic reaction often triggered by medications such as ciprofloxacin. The presence of eosinophilia (12% eosinophils) and the timing of the reaction after starting ciprofloxacin also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
rejected.why: While Stevens-Johnson syndrome is a severe skin and mucous membrane disorder, it typically involves more extensive mucosal involvement and is often associated with a more rapid onset of symptoms.

rejected.label: Acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by numerous small, sterile pustules on the skin, which is not the primary presentation in this case.

rejected.label: Drug-induced liver injury
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin levels, this diagnosis alone does not account for the skin lesions and other systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
rejected.why: Toxic epidermal necrolysis is a severe skin condition with extensive skin necrosis and detachment, which is not the primary presentation in this case.
